name: Psychological Detachment
summary: Mentally switching off from work during non-work time, which is one of the strongest predictors of recovery from job stress.
explanation:
Psychological detachment means being away from work in your head, not only physically. You do not think about tasks, answer messages, or replay problems during your evening, weekend or holiday.

Sabine Sonnentag and Charlotte Fritz made detachment one of four recovery experiences, next to relaxation, mastery and control. Across many diary and longitudinal studies, people who detach more report less exhaustion, better sleep, better mood and more engagement the next day. Their stressor-detachment model adds a trap: high job demands make detachment harder exactly when it is most needed, so stress and poor recovery reinforce each other.

Detachment is attention residue at the scale of the workday. Unfinished tasks and open loops follow you home and keep the work mind running. Things that help: a shutdown ritual that captures open loops and writes the next steps for tomorrow, physical or digital boundaries (no work apps on the personal phone), and absorbing non-work activities that leave no room for work thoughts, such as sport, music or social time.

Detachment is not the same as disengagement. The goal is not to care less about work during work hours, but to let the mind fully leave it afterwards so it can come back rested.
